facts.fact: TechAfrica News reports that the government introduced its personal data legal framework in 2023 through Ordinance-Law No. 23/010, the Digital Code, which sets out lawful processing, transparency, data minimisation and system security, and treats it as the framework within which DPOs ensure compliance; the report gives no date for the statement, so the published date of 2026-03-17 is used.

The Ministry of Digital Economy launched a national Data Protection Officers (DPO) network in Kinshasa to build professional capacity and promote best practice in personal data protection, with Minister Augustin Kibassa Maliba presiding; no sanction or decision is reported; the report gives no event date, so the published date of 2026-03-17 is used.

The report says the DPO network forms part of the national data governance effort 'aligned with ... plans to establish a dedicated Data Protection Authority', so the authority is planned and not yet established; no date is given for the statement, so the published date of 2026-03-17 is used.

facts.fact: We Are Tech Africa reports that the DPO network comes three years after adoption of ordonnance-loi n°23/010 on the Digital Code, which sets the principles of lawful, transparent and secure processing of personal data and under which DPOs operate; the report gives no separate date for the statement, so the published date of 2026-03-16 is used.

On Thursday 12 March 2026 in Kinshasa the Ministry of Digital Economy launched the national network of data protection officers, to standardise personal data practice and support compliance in the public and private sectors, backed by RUDI International and Droit-Numérique.cd; no sanction or decision is reported.

The Minister of Digital Economy says the DPO network precedes the 'création prochaine' of a national Data Protection Authority, so the authority is not yet created; the published date of 2026-03-16 is used.

facts.fact: Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 of 13 March 2023 on the Digital Code was made by the President; its Book III sets the rules on public data and the protection of personal data (Article 166); the passages read contain no commencement provision, so only enactment is recorded.

Article 262 creates an independent administrative Autorité de protection des données with legal personality and administrative and financial autonomy, and says a Prime Minister's decree will fix its organisation and functioning; Articles 267 to 268 set the membership conditions and a four-member bureau; the document does not show it constituted.

facts.fact: The Droit-Numérique.cd analysis states that Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 of 13 March 2023 on the Digital Code, which provides for the Autorité de Protection des Données, entered into force in 2023; the document gives no more exact date for entry into force, so the year is recorded.

The analysis states that Articles 262 to 270 of the Digital Code provide for the Autorité de Protection des Données, to be set up by Prime Ministerial decree, and that a ministerial order of 17 August 2024 (n° CAB/MIN/PT&N/AKIM/KL/KBS/051/2024) provisionally transferred its missions to ARPTIC pending its establishment; the document does not say ARPTIC has acted in that role.

facts.fact: ACTPOL, citing the African Union status list of 2 February 2026, says the DRC has ratified the Malabo Convention.
Africa Data Protection reports the ARPTC has exercised the data protection authority's missions provisionally since March 2023, while the authority the Digital Code provides for is not yet installed.
Africa Data Protection reports the Digital Code's prior-formalities regime was set by ARPTC Decision n° 039/ARPTC/CLG/2025, published in the Journal officiel on 23 April 2026.
The ARPTC president marked two years of application of Ordonnance-Loi No 23/010 of 13 March 2023 on the Code du numerique, which he says sets rules for personal data processing.
The ARPTC president said a ministerial order of 17 August 2024 provisionally entrusted the ARPTC with personal data protection.

facts.fact: Think Tank Law and Technologies' study, presented 6 August 2024, treats the digital code's personal data rules as the law in force.
Think Tank Law and Technologies said on 6 August 2024 that the authority created by article 262 of the digital code still has to be made operational by decree.
UNESCO reports that a 12-13 August 2025 Kinshasa workshop examined the legal texts in force on personal data protection, including Ordonnance-loi no 23/010 of 13 March 2023, the Code du Numerique.
Levellers says the Digital Code (Ordonnance-loi 23/010) with personal data rules in Book III is in force since 11 April 2023.
Levellers says the DRC deposited its Malabo Convention ratification instrument at Addis Ababa on 27 June 2025, becoming the 17th state party.
Levellers says the data protection authority provided for in Article 262 of the Digital Code has not been established and is not operational as of June 2026.
